exposure: no immediate newborn skin-to-skin contact after birth
gave birth at home or in the village
cohort: The study included a total weighted sample of 4748 women aged 15-49 years from Papua New Guinea, derived from the 2016-2018 PNG Demographic and Health Survey.
finding: Approximately one in four women (24.6%) in Papua New Guinea delayed initiation of breastfeeding, with factors like unplanned pregnancy, caesarean section, and lack of immediate skin-to-skin contact significantly increasing the odds of delay.
mod_finding: Women who had a caesarean section had significantly higher odds (AOR 3.16) of delayed breastfeeding initiation compared to those with other birth modes.
cross-section timing: Data was collected between 2016-2018 for the PNG Demographic and Health Survey.
